mainTopic: Sources for שליחות, the princes' פסוק and the court-appointed guardian for orphans
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא. There, רבי יונתן learns from 'ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל' that all of ישראל can be יוצא with one קרבן פסח. So the גמרא asks where he learns שליח בקדשים. It settles on 'ויקחו להם איש שה לבית אבת שה לבית', whose double wording teaches שליחות even for someone with no share in the offering. It then defends that source: רבי יצחק's rule comes from 'איש לפי אכלו', and רבי יונתן holds a פסח is not slaughtered for one person alone. Next the גמרא asks why רב doesn't learn שליחות from the princes who divided ארץ ישראל. It answers that minors cannot take part in שליחות. A land portion may also be unwanted, so it is not a simple case of זכין לאדם שלא בפניו. Instead the princes teach that בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס for orphans, who may cause a loss for the sake of a gain. Finally, שמואל rules that grown orphans can protest the court's division, while רב נחמן says they cannot, because of 'מה כח בית דין יפה'. The גמרא challenges רב נחמן from a משנה about judges' appraisals and begins its answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: All of Israel can fulfill their obligation with one Paschal offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its teaching: since one person does the שחיטה, 'the whole congregation slaughters' must mean all of ישראל can be יוצא with one קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know all of ישראל can fulfill their obligation with one פסח? The פסוק says 'the whole congregation of ישראל shall slaughter it.' Does the whole congregation slaughter? Only one person slaughters! So this teaches that all of ישראל can fulfill their obligation with one פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that explains how רבי יונתן uses the פסוק 'ושחטו אותו כל קהל עדת ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says everyone slaughters, but in reality only one person does the שחיטה. So the extra wording is read as a new law: one קרבן פסח can cover all of ישראל. This matters because it means רבי יונתן has 'used up' this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The Paschal offering brought on ערב פסח

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The question 'from where do we know all of ישראל are יוצא with one פסח' began just before this.

phrases.english: [From where do we know all of Israel fulfill their obligation] with one Paschal offering?
As it is said: 'And they shall slaughter it,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל קְהַל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel, in the afternoon.'
Does the whole assembly, all of them, slaughter?
But only one person slaughters!
Rather, from here we learn that all of Israel
fulfill their obligation with one Paschal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִכָּאן שֶׁכׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאִים בְּפֶסַח אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that explains רבי יונתן's use of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of ישראל can be יוצא with one קרבן פסח, learned from 'כל קהל עדת ישראל'.

steps.title: Then where does רבי יונתן learn agency for offerings?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יונתן uses the פסוק for 'one פסח for all', the גמרא asks where he gets the law of שליח בקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Agency for offerings, where does he learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question: if this פסוק is used for something else, what is רבי יונתן's source for שליחות in קדשים? This sets up the search for a source in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Others learned שליח בקדשים from this very פסוק. Since רבי יונתן uses it for a different law, he needs another source.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who acts for someone else
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: Agency regarding offerings, from where does he derive it?
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבי יונתן, whose view the ברייתא was explaining.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 1: the פסוק is used up, so a new source is needed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יונתן's source for שליחות in קדשים

steps.title: From the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יונתן learns שליחות from that same פסוק too.
steps.simpleTranslation: From it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same פסוק teaches agency as well, because one person slaughters for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One person doing the שחיטה for the whole group shows that one can act for others in קדשים. So the פסוק can teach both laws.

phrases.english: From it.
phrases.notes: From the same פסוק, 'ושחטו אותו', since one person slaughters for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same פסוק of 'ושחטו אותו' also teaches שליחות.

steps.title: Rejected: the slaughterer is a partner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the one slaughtering owns a share in the קרבן פסח, so that may not count as true שליחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it is different there, because he has a partnership with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3. The slaughterer is himself a partner in the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partner is partly acting for himself, not only for others. So this case cannot prove that a שליח with no share can act for someone.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since he has partnership with them.
phrases.notes: The slaughterer has his own share in the same פסח animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'ושחטו אותו' as a source for full שליחות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The slaughterer is a שותף, so he may be acting partly for himself.

steps.title: A new source: 'a lamb for a household'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different source: 'ויקחו להם איש שה לבית אבת שה לבית'. One man takes a lamb for the whole house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from here: 'And they shall take to them every man a lamb, for the fathers' house, a lamb for a household.'
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first source, the גמרא brings a new פסוק to show שליחות in קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows one man taking a lamb on behalf of his whole household. That is one person acting for others.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'And they shall take to them every man a lamb, for the fathers' house,'
'a lamb for a household.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שליחות in קדשים comes from 'ויקחו להם איש שה לבית אבת שה לבית'.

steps.title: Same problem: maybe he is a partner here too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the man taking the lamb is also a partner in it, so the same rejection should apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps there too, it is because he has a partnership with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same objection from step 4 against the new source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who takes the lamb also eats from it, so he is a שותף. That would again fail to prove agency for someone with no share.

phrases.english: But perhaps there too,
it is because he has partnership with them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the objection of step 4 to the source of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'ויקחו להם' in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The taker is a שותף in the lamb, so the case may not be true agency.

steps.title: Two verses teach agency even without partnership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah says this in two פסוקים. The extra one is applied to a case of a שליח who is not a partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need two verses? If it does not apply to where it belongs, apply it to where it does not belong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof: having two פסוקים for the same idea shows it must be teaching something beyond the partner case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both פסוקים (ושחטו אתו and ויקחו להם) only taught the partner case, one would be extra. So the extra one is moved to the case it doesn't naturally fit: a שליח with no share in the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two verses?
If it is not needed for its own topic (apply it elsewhere)

steps.whatToRemember: An extra, repeated phrase in a פסוק is used to teach the case it doesn't naturally fit. Here that is a שליח with no share in the offering.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need two verses?
phrases.notes: The פסוק says it twice: 'a lamb for the fathers' house' and 'a lamb for a household.'

phrases.english: If it is not needed for where he belongs [as a partner],
apply it to where he does not belong [has no share].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording (אם אינו ענין) applied to a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only shows a partner acting for others.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeated phrase teaches שליחות even for one with no share.

steps.title: Isn't the verse needed for רבי יצחק's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the word 'איש' in this פסוק is needed for רבי יצחק's rule that an adult can acquire for others but a minor cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is needed for the teaching of רבי יצחק, for רבי יצחק said: A 'man' can acquire, but a minor cannot acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source from step 5 by saying it is already used for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'איש' teaches that only an adult can acquire on behalf of others, the פסוק may not be free to teach שליחות. A פסוק already used for one law can't easily be used for another.

phrases.english: This is needed for him for the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak.
For Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A 'man' acquires [for others], but a minor does not acquire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source of steps 5 and 7 from a new angle
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'ויקחו להם איש' for שליחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used for רבי יצחק's rule, so it is not free for שליחות.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's rule comes from 'every man according to his eating'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יצחק's rule comes from a different phrase, 'איש לפי אכלו'. So 'ויקחו להם' stays free to teach שליחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is derived from 'every man according to his eating.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving רבי יצחק's rule to a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'איש לפי אכלו' teaches that only an adult acquires for others, 'ויקחו להם' is not needed for that. So it remains the source for שליח בקדשים.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יונתן, שליח בקדשים comes from 'ויקחו להם איש שה לבית אבת שה לבית'. רבי יצחק's rule that only an adult acquires for others comes from 'איש לפי אכלו'.

phrases.english: That is derived from 'every man according to his eating.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the competing law to a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויקחו להם איש' is used up by רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יצחק's rule comes from 'איש לפי אכלו', so 'ויקחו להם' is free to teach שליחות.

steps.title: The phrase is still needed for a Pesach for one person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that איש לפי אכלו is needed to teach that a קרבן פסח may be slaughtered for a single person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that phrase is still needed to teach that you can slaughter a קרבן פסח for one person alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. The phrase איש לפי אכלו is not free to teach רבי יצחק's rule, because it is needed for another law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the גמרא moved רבי יצחק's rule onto איש לפי אכלו. Now it says that phrase already teaches that one person alone may bring a קרבן פסח. If so, רבי יצחק's rule has no source again, and ויקחו להם would be needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And still / but still (introduces a further problem)
He needs it (the phrase is already used for something else)
We slaughter the קרבן פסח for a single person

phrases.english: But he still needs it
phrases.notes: "It" is the phrase איש לפי אכלו from the last step.

phrases.english: to teach that one may slaughter the Pesach offering for an individual.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 by claiming איש לפי אכלו is already used for another law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that איש לפי אכלו is free to teach רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A phrase already used for one law cannot also teach a second law, so רבי יצחק's rule would again need ויקחו להם.

steps.title: He holds a Pesach is not slaughtered for one person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן holds the opinion that a קרבן פסח may not be slaughtered for one person alone, so the phrase איש לפי אכלו is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the opinion that says we do not slaughter a קרבן פסח for one person alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The one who learns שליחות from ויקחו להם simply does not hold the law about one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת whether a קרבן פסח may be brought for one person. רבי יונתן takes the side that says no, so איש לפי אכלו is not used for that law. It stays free for רבי יצחק's rule, and ויקחו להם stays free to teach שליחות.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like the one who says (sides with a known opinion)

phrases.english: He holds like the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
phrases.english: One may not slaughter the Pesach offering for an individual.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by placing the author on the side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the author to one side of a dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איש לפי אכלו is taken up by the law that a Pesach may be brought for one person.
steps.terutzMaskana: This author holds a Pesach is not brought for one person, so the phrase is free for רבי יצחק's rule.

steps.title: Why not learn agency from the tribal princes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב גידל in the name of רב, who learns שליחות from the princes who divided the land. Why not use that source instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב גידל said in the name of רב: How do we know a person's agent is like himself? From the פסוק 'one prince from each tribe.' So learn שליחות from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a whole different source for שליחות. It asks why we needed all the earlier sources if this one exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each tribe's prince took land for everyone in his tribe, which looks like a שליח acting for others. If this פסוק teaches שליחות, the earlier struggle with ויקחו להם and other פסוקים seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's agent is like himself
Let him derive it (from this other source)

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: But what about that which Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that a person's agent is like himself?
As it says: "And one prince,
one prince from each tribe."
Let him derive agency from here!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending ויקחו להם, the גמרא challenges the whole search by pointing to another source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the earlier sources of שליחות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב already learns שליחות from the princes, the other derivations seem unnecessary.

steps.title: The princes cannot be agents because minors cannot appoint agents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the princes were שלוחים, because the princes took land for minors too, and minors cannot make a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think this was שליחות? Minors cannot appoint an agent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the princes' role cannot be שליחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The princes took land for every member of the tribe, including children. A קטן cannot appoint a שליח. So the princes were acting through some other legal mechanism, and this פסוק cannot be the source for שליחות.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you understand this? (introduces a rejection)
People who can take part in agency

phrases.english: And can you really think that this was agency?
But minors
are not able to take part in agency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by showing the princes' case cannot be שליחות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the proposed source does not fit the concept
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The princes were שלוחים of their tribes, so the פסוק teaches שליחות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since minors cannot appoint a שליח, the princes acted through a different mechanism.

steps.title: The princes teach acting for someone's benefit when he is not there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק of the princes fits a different rule of רבא בר רב הונא: one may acquire something for a person's benefit when he is not present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it fits what רבא בר רב הונא said in the name of רב גידל in the name of רב: How do we know you can acquire for a person when he is not there? From 'one prince, one prince.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the princes are not שלוחים, the גמרא offers another way to explain what they did. It suggests they acted for everyone's benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זכין לאדם שלא בפניו does not need appointment, so it works even for minors. The princes would be acquiring land as a benefit for each member of the tribe.

keyTerms.meaning: One may acquire for a person when he is not present (when it benefits him)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כִּי הָא דְּרָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rather, it is like that teaching of Rava bar Rav Huna,
for Rava bar Rav Huna said
that Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that one may acquire for a person when he is not present?
As it says: "And one prince, one prince."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי הָא דְּרָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the פסוק is not about שליחות, the גמרא proposes it teaches a different rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The princes' acquiring land teaches זכין לאדם שלא בפניו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different law
steps.terutzMaskana: The princes' פסוק teaches זכין לאדם שלא בפניו, which needs no appointment and so works for minors. Step 15 challenges this.

steps.title: A land portion may not be a benefit for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that getting a land portion is not purely a benefit, since some people want hill land and some want valley land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really call it a benefit? It can also be a loss. Some people want land on a hill and not in a valley, and some want land in a valley and not on a hill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from step 14. The princes were not clearly helping everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זכין לאדם שלא בפניו only works when the act is clearly good for the person. A prince choosing land for someone might give him the kind of land he does not want, so it can be a חוב (loss). That breaks the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: It is pleasing to him / he prefers it

phrases.english: And can you really think it is a benefit?
There is also a disadvantage,
for there is someone who prefers land on a hill
and does not want land in a valley,
and there is someone who prefers land in a valley
and does not want land on a hill!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the princes acted under זכין לאדם שלא בפניו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule needs a clear benefit, but a land portion may be unwanted, so it can be a loss.

steps.title: The princes teach the court-appointed guardian for orphans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבא בר רב הונא: when orphans divide their father's property, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס who acts both to their loss and to their gain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like what רבא בר רב הונא said in the name of רב גידל in the name of רב: How do we know that when orphans come to divide their father's property, בית דין appoints a guardian for them, to their loss and to their gain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the princes' role. This step starts quoting רב's statement, and the quote is completed in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The princes are now compared to an אפוטרופוס, who is appointed by authority and can act even when a choice is not purely a benefit. This handles the hill-versus-valley problem from step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: A guardian / steward appointed to manage someone's affairs
To cause loss and to cause gain

phrases.english: Rather, it is like Rava bar Rav Huna's other teaching,
for Rava bar Rav Huna said
that Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know, for orphans who came
to divide their father's property,
that the court appoints a guardian for them
to act to their loss and to their gain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by giving the princes' פסוק a different meaning that allows acting to someone's loss.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The princes acted only for a clear benefit, and that fails when a portion may be unwanted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The princes were like a court-appointed אפוטרופוס, who may act even where there is some loss.

steps.title: Why would a guardian act to their loss?
steps.stepSummary: In the middle of the quote, the גמרא asks why a guardian would be appointed to cause the orphans a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: "To their loss"? Why would that be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the quote to ask about one strange word. It is setting up a clarification of what "to their loss" means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין protects orphans, so appointing someone just to hurt them makes no sense. The גמרא wants the wording explained before finishing the quote.

phrases.english: "To their loss" — why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a word inside the statement quoted in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What it means that the guardian is appointed "to their loss."

steps.title: A loss that leads to a gain, learned from the princes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the guardian may cause a loss in order to bring a gain, and then finishes רב's statement with the source: the פסוק of the princes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a loss in order to bring a gain. The פסוק teaches this: "And one prince, one prince from each tribe you shall take."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies the word "loss" and then completes רב's quote by giving the פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guardian may make a choice that hurts the orphans in one way if it helps them overall. A prince choosing hill or valley land for his tribe is the same kind of authority, so the פסוק teaches the אפוטרופוס rule, not שליחות.

keyTerms.meaning: In order to bring a gain

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of the princes is not the source for שליחות, since minors cannot appoint a שליח. It is also not a simple case of זכין לאדם שלא בפניו, since a land portion might be unwanted. It teaches that בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס for orphans, who may cause a short-term loss for their overall gain.
steps.confusionAlert: "To their loss" does not mean the guardian may harm the orphans. It means he may accept a smaller loss as part of a step that benefits them overall.

phrases.english: Rather, read it: "to their loss in order to bring a gain."
The verse teaches:
"And one prince, one prince
from each tribe you shall take."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and completes the statement begun in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Loss" means a loss made in order to bring an overall gain, and the source is the פסוק of the princes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The princes' פסוק teaches the court-appointed guardian for orphans, so it does not compete with the sources for שליחות.

steps.title: שמואל: Orphans who grow up can protest the division
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: when orphans divide their father's property, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס who picks a good portion for each one. Once the orphans grow up, they may protest the division.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: If orphans come to divide their father's property, the court appoints a guardian for them, and he chooses a good portion for each of them. If they grow up, they can protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from שמואל about how orphans divide their father's estate. It also says what happens once the orphans grow up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court steps in because the orphans are too young to divide the property themselves. שמואל adds that this division is not final: once the orphans grow up, they can object and ask for a new division.

keyTerms.meaning: A guardian appointed to manage someone else's affairs

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
Orphans who came to divide
their father's property:
the court appoints a guardian for them,
and they choose for them a fine portion,
and if they grew up, they can protest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of a guardian dividing orphans' property, which was raised in step 16. It now asks whether the division is final.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans who grow up may protest the court's division of their father's estate.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Orphans who grow up cannot protest
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives his own view: once the orphans grow up they cannot protest. Otherwise, what power would בית דין have?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן himself said: If they grow up, they cannot protest. For if they could, what strength would the court's power have?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן disagrees with the teaching he just quoted from שמואל. He says the court's division stays final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is "מה כח בית דין יפה": a decision of בית דין must carry more weight than a private deal. If the orphans could undo the division later, the court's authority would mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the advantage of the court's power? (the court's rulings must have special force)

steps.whyThisMatters: This reasoning, "מה כח בית דין יפה", is exactly what the גמרא will question in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said his own view:
if they grew up, they cannot protest,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה?
phrases.english: for if so, what is the strength of the court's power?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to שמואל's ruling in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grown orphans cannot protest the division, because a court's actions must have binding force.

steps.title: Does רב נחמן really hold this reasoning? A challenge from judges' appraisals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב נחמן really accepts "מה כח בית דין יפה". In a משנה about judges who misjudged a property's value by a sixth, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses this very reasoning to keep the sale. Yet רב נחמן rules like the חכמים, who cancel the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב נחמן really hold "if so, what is the strength of the court's power"? But we learned in a משנה: When judges appraise property and go a sixth too low or a sixth too high, their sale is void. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Their sale stands, for if not, what is the strength of the court's power? And רב הונא בר חיננא said in the name of רב נחמן: The הלכה follows the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן. In another case he rules against the very reasoning he used here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses "מה כח בית דין יפה" to uphold the court's sale. The חכמים reject it and cancel the sale. Since רב נחמן rules like the חכמים, it seems he does not accept this reasoning, which contradicts what he said in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה follows the majority חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "מה כח בית דין יפה" belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, not the חכמים. Ruling like the חכמים means rejecting that reasoning, at least in that case.

phrases.english: And does Rav Nachman really hold

phrases.aramaic: ״אִם כֵּן מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה״?
phrases.english: "if so, what is the strength of the court's power"?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
The appraisal of the judges
who went down a sixth or went up a sixth,
phrases.notes: The judges set the price a sixth below or above the property's real value when selling it.

phrases.english: their sale is void.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִכְרָן קַיָּים.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Their sale stands.
(And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, the next line is still his reason.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן – מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה!
phrases.english: If so, what is the strength of the court's power!

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Huna bar Chinnana said that Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן אִם כֵּן מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning רב נחמן gave in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's use of "מה כח בית דין יפה" to rule that grown orphans cannot protest.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן rules like the חכמים against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the one who relies on "מה כח בית דין יפה". That shows he rejects this reasoning, so he contradicts himself.

steps.title: No difficulty: the answer begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says "לא קשיא": there is no real contradiction in רב נחמן's views. The explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that it will resolve the contradiction. This line sets up the answer, which comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא קשיא" signals that the two rulings of רב נחמן can both stand. The גמרא will show how the two cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (the details come next)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן seemed to contradict himself about "מה כח בית דין יפה".
steps.terutzMaskana: The contradiction will be resolved; the explanation follows.
